title: Weight-Space Programming for Materials Science
read_level: full main text (Sec. 1-6) and supplementary S3 (reading/editing experiments); per-task supplementary prompt/reply listings skimmed
why_wsp: Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.2, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 each write every weight of a zero-initialized 16-hidden-unit MLP as text from a task description and named inputs, with no labels, tools or code; networks are then used as label-free predictors and GP/BNN prior means in materials discovery.
domain: materials discovery: alloy properties, Thermo-Calc phase equilibria, crystal bulk modulus/heat capacity, Bayesian optimization, generative crystal screening
editor: Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.2 (all tasks), Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 (alloy and crystal tasks)
target: MLP with one hidden layer of 16 ReLU units, "16𝑑 + 33 weights, which for the tasks here is 113 to 417 numbers"; larger variants 577 to 1,825 weights; S3: a 51-32-32-1 trained network, last-layer readouts of MACE/ORB/eSEN/GRACE (128/256/128/64 weights)
interface: direct values (decimal numbers under one header per tensor, no code execution)
loop: one-shot for written networks (fresh session, no execution); S3.2 feedback arm: closed-loop with five attempts
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: All weights written from zero; "a typical reply uses 5 or 6 of the 16 hidden units on the experimental alloys and the Thermo-Calc targets and 10 on crystals (medians)" (Sec. 4)

headline_results.quote: On the five experimental alloy tasks Opus 5.5 reaches 𝜌 = 0.64 to 0.79 and Fable 5.2 0.51 to 0.76.
the Opus networks are ahead of the best of these descriptors on every task, by 0.04 to 0.17
all 35 targets the Opus networks rank the pool at a mean 𝜌 = 0.67 and the Fable networks at 0.64

headline_results.claim: GP prior mean at five labels
headline_results.quote: they raise the ranking at five labels from 0.35 to 0.69 on alloys and from 0.15 to 0.95 on crystals
the Opus networks lower the regret significantly on 16 and raise it on none
The written filter therefore matches what 400 labeled crystals give a standard model and does not exceed it

headline_results.claim: Good pool ranking can still mislead optimizer
headline_results.quote: still make the optimization worse than with no prior, in 14 of 20 seeds
We found no case in which a model extracted from trained weights something that a simple statistic of those weights missed.

cost.quote: a reply from Opus 5.5 took a median of about 4 minutes and 73,000 output tokens, almost all of it reasoning. Fable 5.2 took under a minute and about 9,400 tokens

baselines_and_controls: Label-free references: rule of mixtures, atomic size mismatch and three other descriptors (alloys), inverse volume per atom and Dulong-Petit (crystals), Redlich-Kister-Muggianu sub-system extrapolation (Thermo-Calc); plain constant-mean GP; models trained on 400 labeled crystals (same-size network, ridge, random forest); S3: weight statistics, line search, SPSA, (1+1)-ES, gradient fit.
runs_and_variance: Two or three replies per model and task (358 runs audited); BO uses "20 seeds per arm" with paired Wilcoxon and Holm correction; crystal tasks six/five non-independent runs; authors note significance "says nothing about the variation between replies".
robustness_of_edits: not tested for fine-tuning/quantization; distribution shift: crystal surrogate trained on DFT labels, tested on potential-labelled generated crystals; gain confined to first tens of labels
verification: none formal; statistical tests (Wilcoxon, Holm); transcripts audited for tool calls ("all 358 runs behind the main text passed")
memorization_vs_reasoning: Explicitly discussed: "the experimental results measure recall as well as reasoning"; computed Thermo-Calc targets added because they are "unlikely to have been seen as a table"; self-reports show "calibration against remembered values of alloys that are in the pools".
limitations_stated: Single vendor's models; possible recall of public datasets; tool-use exclusion by instruction and audit not technical block; Thermo-Calc targets from one software version; fixed pools 152-722 candidates; one network size and prompt wording; crystal runs share starting set.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog)
notes_for_survey: Writing-mode WSP as a zero-label prior for materials discovery, with strong label-free references (sub-system extrapolation) that the networks only roughly match on smooth targets. Supplementary S3 reports reading and editing modes as less successful: LLMs did not beat a simple weight statistic in locating a planted leak, and readout edits with feedback matched but did not exceed a gradient fit.
